1.0.0.en: The saints: those set apart for Christ, that is, the Christian believers.

1.0.1.en: God chose Paul to be His servant, as He declared to Ananias (Acts 9:15), and he sends this epistle to the Christians in Ephesus.

1.1.0.en: Paul sends his good wishes to the Church of Ephesus for the work of divine grace in them. This includes all the blessings, which he sums up in the peace that fills their hearts. They receive these blessings from the Father and the Son, which shows the equality of the hypostases together.

1.1.1.en: May you begin your words with others with wishes of blessing for them or words of praise, so that their hearts rejoice and they are thereby ready to hear the rest of what you say.

1.2.0.en: Blessed: worthy of praise and thanksgiving. The Father of our Lord: he speaks of the Father who created us and gave us all blessings, and of Christ His Son, who became incarnate for our redemption. So he speaks of the hypostases of the Father and the Son.

1.2.1.en: In heavenly places: the spiritual blessings that He gave to the heavenly ones and gives us a share of on earth. In Christ: we receive these blessings through Christ the Redeemer, and they include the Holy Sacraments and all the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church.

1.2.2.en: Paul begins his discourse by thanking God for the spiritual blessings that He granted to the believers in the Church.

1.3.0.en: Chosen us: by God's foreknowledge and love He knows who will believe in Christ, so before He created us He chose us in order to give us His blessings. This produces humility in us, because He is the cause of our blessing and not we ourselves. In Him: in Christ the Redeemer, in whom we will believe and receive salvation.

1.3.1.en: Before the foundation of the world: that is, in God's intention even before He created any human being, for He loves us and wants to bless us.

1.3.2.en: Holy: set apart for His love and for a life of holiness and righteousness with Him.

1.3.3.en: Without blame: without sin, so that we live in purity.

1.3.4.en: In love: the love of God, which created us, gives to us and helps us toward holiness.

1.3.5.en: St. Paul the Apostle makes clear a second reason for thanking God, namely His love, shown in choosing us before He created us, to be His children and to be sanctified in Him. The purpose of our existence in life is holiness and enjoying fellowship with God.

1.4.0.en: Predestinated us unto adoption: He chose us to become His beloved children.

1.4.1.en: By Jesus Christ: but the basis of this sonship is faith in His only-begotten Son Jesus Christ and the second birth of Baptism.

1.4.2.en: According to the good pleasure of His will: God rejoices in the sonship of His children, in their belonging to Him, their obedience and their blessing Him. God's aim in choosing us is not only to save us from our sins and the sentence of death, but that we become His children and so enjoy all the blessings of His fatherhood.

1.4.3.en: How great is the grace of sonship that God has given us! May we use it to draw near to Him and enjoy fellowship with Him, and at the same time keep away from the evils of the world by keeping His commandments and cutting off the causes of sin, however prevalent they are in the world or dear to us.

1.5.0.en: When we become children of God by adoption, this makes us praise Him, thank Him and extol His glorious grace, which He bestowed on us in honor of Christ. At the time of the baptism in the Jordan and at the time of the Transfiguration, "the Beloved" was the title by which the Father named Him: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 17:5). The Father loved the Son, and by our union with the Son we too have become beloved of the Father, and He has lavished His grace upon us.

1.6.0.en: Wisdom: right conduct at the right time.

1.6.1.en: Prudence: the skill of God. He accomplished redemption for us by the blood of Christ, and by this redemption we have the forgiveness of sins. This free redemption showed us the abundance of God's love, which flows from His countless treasures, and this grace also gave us wisdom and prudence generously.

1.7.0.en: Which He purposed in Himself: His desire to redeem mankind by giving Himself for it.

1.7.1.en: The wisdom and prudence with which God favored us made it possible for us to know God's purpose, which is the redemption of His people. This purpose was hidden in former times, but has now been made known by the favor of His grace and by the wisdom and prudence He gave us. This purpose and this justification came about without anyone's counsel.

1.8.0.en: The fullness of times: the time in which Christ became incarnate.

1.8.1.en: God ordered the times and seasons for the carrying out of His purpose, which is the accomplishment of the mystery of redemption, in order to gather together the believers, the members of the body of Christ. Christ is the head of all, and He is the head of the Church, and so that reconciliation might be accomplished by the blood of the Cross between those on earth and those in heaven.

1.9.0.en: In whom: that is, in Christ.

1.9.1.en: An inheritance: God gives us a portion in His Church through the Holy Sacraments and the work of the Holy Spirit in us.

1.9.2.en: Predestinated: by the ordering of God's eternal love for us.

1.9.3.en: Who works all things: God who works in all His children.

1.9.4.en: The counsel of His will: that is, His fatherhood, which ordered our salvation.

1.9.5.en: God has loved us from eternity and ordered our salvation in the fullness of time by the redemption on the Cross, and we receive this salvation in the Church by the grace of the Holy Spirit, through the Holy Sacraments and all spiritual things.

1.9.6.en: May we thank God every day for what we receive in our spiritual and bodily life, so that we feel the value of His gifts and enjoy them more and more.

1.10.s.en: (4) The Holy Spirit for all believers

1.10.0.en: God gave us these gifts to be a means of praising and glorifying His majesty. "We" here refers to the Christian believers of Jewish origin, who had the promises and believed in the Christ promised in their Scriptures, for they had learned from the prophecies of the Old Testament to expect the coming of Christ.

1.11.0.en: In whom: that is, in Christ.

1.11.1.en: You also: the believers from among the Gentiles.

1.11.2.en: The word of truth: the Gospel, with all the teachings it contains, is truth, and there is in it nothing of Jewish tradition or Greek philosophy; it is the truth that brought salvation.

1.11.3.en: Sealed: by your faith in Christ God has marked you as set apart for Him, and you received the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in you through the sacrament of the Holy Myron.

1.11.4.en: Paul addresses the Christians in Ephesus who were of Gentile origin and tells them that when they accepted the proclamation of the Gospel and believed it, they deserved to receive the permanent indwelling of the Holy Spirit in them.

1.12.0.en: The earnest of our inheritance: an earnest is a part of the price paid in advance, and it points to the spiritual blessings that we receive in the Church, which are a sample of the glories and blessings that we will receive in heaven. The purchased possession: the believers in Christ whom He purchased with His blood.

1.12.1.en: Paul makes clear that what the believers receive in the Church of the Holy Spirit, in the form of the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace such as prayers and meditations on the Holy Bible, is the earnest of what we will receive in eternity. For these blessings that He gives to His people whom He purchased with His blood, that is, His Church, we thank Him and glorify Him for these gifts.

1.12.2.en: The Holy Spirit works in the Church and is ready to give you as much as you desire. In proportion to your attachment to the Church and your submission to the work of the Holy Spirit, you will enjoy Him, and even taste moments of spiritual feelings higher than the moments of this age, for they are a small light from eternity that you see on earth.

1.13.0.en: The saints: the believers. Paul heard of the faith of the Church of Ephesus and its love for all the believers, so he always gives thanks to God for the spiritual gifts He has bestowed on them, and prays, asking for all good things for them.

1.14.0.en: The God of our Lord Jesus: of course the Father is not God to the Son, since the two are one in essence. But the expression here means that Christ, in His incarnation and when He took on our humanity, became subject to the Father. Paul does not mean to diminish the divinity of the Lord Christ, since he himself said, "Great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh ... preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory" (1 Tim 3:16). The spirit of wisdom: that is, the Holy Spirit, who distinguishes all things.

1.14.1.en: The revelation in the knowledge of Him: that is, the disclosure of truths about God to the believing human being and the showing of His work in His creation. In this verse Paul brings together the three hypostases: the Father sent His Son in the form of weakness to redeem mankind and then raise it in Him to heavenly glory, and from Him proceeds the Holy Spirit, who binds the believers to God.

1.15.0.en: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened: you believe and see what human eyes do not see.

1.15.1.en: The hope of His calling: the hope in the Kingdom of Heaven which the Gospel proclaims.

1.15.2.en: The riches of the glory of His inheritance: the greatness of the eternal glories.

1.15.4.en: The Apostle asks for the Christians in Ephesus that they believe the good news, so that they may see with the eye of faith the hope in eternity and its great glories, which God gives to all who believe in Him.

1.16.0.en: The Apostle shows how great is the power of the Holy Spirit working in the believers, and he expresses His power with the words "greatness ... exceeding ... mighty", to show the power of the Holy Spirit in supporting a person to leave his sins, to be joined to God, to love Him and to grow in knowing Him.

1.16.1.en: Without prayer and asking for God's help the human mind cannot understand the things of God. As the Fathers say, the one who does not love prayer has nothing good in him at all. May you hasten to God in all your needs, and even take care to praise Him and thank Him, so that your knowledge of Him and the longings of your love for Him increase.

1.17.0.en: His right hand: signifies the power and the complete glory that Christ received by His ascension into the heavens as a representative of the human race, to open the way for us.

1.17.1.en: The Apostle makes clear that God, by the power of His Holy Spirit, raised Christ, caused Him to ascend and glorified Him in the heavens, not to glorify the Son in Himself, for He is glorified from eternity with His Father, but as a perfect man. His resurrection signifies our resurrection from sin and encourages us, however far away we may be, for His Holy Spirit is able to draw us and raise us from our weaknesses and give us glories in heaven with Christ our Lord.

1.18.0.en: Not only in this world, but also in that which is to come: that is, not only the rulers and great ones we know in this life, but also what we may see in eternity, for Christ is above all. By Christ's ascension and sitting at the right hand of the Father, He was raised in His humanity above all the ranks of angels, whether "principality" or "power" or "might" or "dominion"; all the angelic orders have come under the authority of Christ. And not only all the ranks of angels, but also above every authority or power in the world of all creatures, in this world and the next.

1.19.0.en: Put all things under His feet: the full realization of which will take place in the final victory of Christ at His second coming (1 Cor 15:24, 25). By the glorification of Christ in His sitting on the heavenly throne He has become head over all things; He is on the throne of the headship of the universe and He is the head of the Church. He raised her to the highest place, and she has the right to sit on the throne with Him when she completes her striving. Thus He gave her authority over all earthly powers, so that if they plot against her, their plots come to nothing. Just as He made the angels serve her, He subjected the demons to her: "the gates of hell shall not prevail against it" (Mt 16:18).

1.20.0.en: The fullness: the Church is filled with the work of the Holy Spirit in her.

1.20.1.en: That filleth all in all: the Holy Spirit fills all the needs of the believer.

1.20.3.en: The Church is the body of Christ, so she lives by His life and is glorified by His glory, and she is filled by the Holy Spirit, who fills all the needs in all the believers. He fills the whole Church because when the believers partake of the Body and Blood of Christ, He unites with all and fills them, and the Holy Spirit within them works in them to fill them at all times according to their response to Him.

1.20.4.en: God wants to fill you and satisfy you and even raise you above all the evils of the world. So know that you are not of this world, that you may leave your sins and separate yourself from all realms of evil to enjoy fellowship with Christ, looking to the Kingdom that awaits you.

1.20.5.en: Christ unites mankind in His Church

2.0.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle describes the state in which the pagan peoples and all the world were before faith, which is a state of spiritual death and separation from life with God.

2.1.1.en: In time past: before faith in Christ.

2.1.2.en: The course of this world: the evil prevailing in the world.

2.1.3.en: The prince of the power of the air: the devil, who is a spirit and the chief of the demons that war against mankind and move in the air surrounding the earth. He is the chief of the evil spread in the air, and not the air itself, which God created.

2.1.4.en: The children of disobedience: those subject to evil, walking in it and far from faith in Christ. The Apostle makes clear that walking in trespasses and sins is according to the spirit of evil, that is, the devil, who is the chief of the powers of darkness that work and move in the air, that is, in the atmosphere surrounding the earth. He is the devil who suggests evil and sins in the minds of men, and he still works to this day in those who are still under his authority, and presents his sins to all people.

2.2.0.en: Among them ... even as others: they are the wicked people of the world, or the children of disobedience.

2.2.1.en: We Jews all, before we believed, walked like them, that is, like the rest of the wicked in the pagan world, before Christ rescued us. We walked according to our fleshly desires, driven by the lusts of the flesh and the evil thoughts that stir the passions. And because of the evil works that we did, we deserved divine wrath and eternal destruction.

2.2.2.en: The transforming grace of God has worked in us, so that we have become of a new nature. Therefore we must use all its possibilities to know God and enjoy fellowship with Him, and not slip into the sins we have left; and if we fall, we rise quickly and renew our mind in the sacrament of repentance and confession.

2.3.0.en: God is not merely merciful but rich in mercy, that is, abounding in mercy (Ps 51:1). And God is love, that is, there is in Him an unlimited love that moves Him toward us with mercy that has no end.

2.4.0.en: God's mercy was expressed in raising us from the spiritual death of sin, though we were not in a state of righteousness or holiness; rather, He loved us while we were His enemies. This is the wonderful divine love with which He loved us and which He showed us by the coming of His Son Jesus Christ in the flesh, His death for us on the Cross and His resurrection from the dead. By the power of Christ's resurrection God raised us from spiritual death, so our resurrection springs from His resurrection. The phrase "by grace ye are saved" is a summary of the work of divine love and mercy toward us. The Apostle tells the believers that they have obtained salvation from sin and resurrection from spiritual death by the grace of God, that is, by favor and kindness and not by merit.

2.5.0.en: God raised us with the resurrection of Christ, and just as Christ sat at the right hand of the Father in the heavenly places, He gave us to be at the right hand of God with Christ. This is by our union with Christ through Holy Communion, so that we have the right, if we abide in Him, to receive a place in the Kingdom. For Christ, by His resurrection, His ascension and His majesty in the heavens, is the representative and delegate of mankind. His resurrection and ascension are the resurrection and ascension of the human believers in Him when they hold fast to Him and the Holy Spirit works in them, until after this life He brings them to the Kingdom. This encourages us to rise from our sins and to hope for eternal life.

2.5.1.en: The grace of God is ready to work in you however great your weakness. Do not be troubled by the repetition of your sins or by your falling into a hard sin, for God's mercy is greater than all your sins, and He is ready to set you free from them however long they have enslaved you. Only persevere with faith in imitating God and in repentance, confident that He is able to raise you above all evil and even to give you the joy of fellowship with Him.

2.6.0.en: The exceeding riches of His grace: expresses the greatness of the work of grace, which surpasses the mind.

2.6.1.en: That in eternity there may be shown, and revealed to all creation and before the angels also, the greatness of His grace in the love of Christ the Redeemer and His longsuffering toward us until we repent, and His encouragement and support of us until at last He gives us salvation in eternity.

2.7.1.en: You have received salvation by the renewal of your nature in Baptism and your union with Christ in the Eucharist. All this is by the work of grace, but on condition of your faith in Christ; and this faith too is a gift and a grace from God, which you accept and respond to and hold fast in continual striving, and so enjoy all its blessings.

2.8.0.en: The salvation you have received is not the result of your works. God has saved you by grace, so that no one may find an occasion for boasting afterward.

2.9.0.en: His workmanship: He created us as human beings and then renewed our creation in the new birth by Baptism.

2.9.1.en: We Christians have been created a second time by Baptism, because we were dead in sin, and Christ raised us and gave us new life by Baptism. The purpose of the new nature is that we do good works of love and holiness and all the works of spiritual striving. These works were in the mind of God before He created and redeemed us, and He prepared them for us that we might walk in them and enjoy fellowship with Him through them. It is clear from this verse and the verse before it that salvation is by the blood of Christ and not by human works. But the grace that gives us salvation must produce good works that we do and strive in; otherwise the absence of good works confirms that we have not received grace and have not responded to it.

2.10.0.en: Made by hands: the circumcision of the Jews was nothing but an outward mark, because true circumcision is the circumcision of the heart.

2.10.1.en: St. Paul asks them to remember their state before faith. He tells them that they were pagans, uncircumcised, that is, the uncircumcised, and therefore outside God's shepherding of His people and God's covenant with them. The Jews called them "the uncircumcision", as a sign that they were not bound by a covenant with God.

2.11.0.en: Without Christ: that is, without hope or expectation of a Christ who would come so that they might obtain salvation through Him.

2.11.1.en: Aliens from the commonwealth of Israel: not of the chosen people of God who shepherds them, that is, Israel. Strangers from the covenants of promise: strangers to the essence of the promise, who is Christ the Redeemer (Acts 13:32). Having no hope: it is hope in salvation by Christ the Redeemer on earth and then complete salvation in the Kingdom.

2.11.2.en: Without God in the world: without knowledge of God or relationship with Him, for they separated themselves from Him by sin and by refusing to know Him.

2.11.3.en: He speaks to the people of Ephesus, who are Gentiles, that is, non-Jews, saying that before faith they had no hope in the awaited Christ the Redeemer and were far from knowing God and enjoying His care.

2.12.0.en: The blood of Christ: which gives us salvation through the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace.

2.12.1.en: In the Old Testament the Jews were near to God by the sign of circumcision and the blood of the sacrifices offered to Him, while the Gentiles were far from Him. In the New Testament the believers, Jews and Gentiles, have become near to God through Baptism and Holy Communion, and members of His body, that is, the Church.

2.13.0.en: Our peace: He gave peace within the believer, so that there is no conflict between his body and his spirit, and peace among all the believers, Jews and Gentiles, for they have become members of one body.

2.13.1.en: Both: the body and the spirit, or the Jews and the Gentiles, or those on earth and those in heaven.

2.13.2.en: The middle wall of partition: which separates the Jews, as a people special to God, from the Gentiles who were far off, so that they became one people. This barrier is also sin, which separated man from God and made a division within man between his soul and his body.

2.13.3.en: There was enmity between the people of ancient Israel and the pagan peoples, and they did not mingle with the rest of the Gentiles, since the Jews regarded the Gentile as unclean, and it was forbidden for the Gentile to approach the temple; there was a high barrier separating the inner court from the court of the Gentiles. But in Christ Jesus all became one, and those on earth were reconciled with those in heaven, and He made both one, making peace for all with one another and between all and God.

2.14.0.en: The enmity: between the Jews and the Gentiles, and between God and man.

2.14.1.en: The ordinances: those which stood in the practices of the people of Israel, such as circumcision, the purifications and not eating certain animals. The Lord Jesus abolished them by His death on the Cross, because they were a type of His sacrifice. Christ, by accomplishing redemption, created one new man, neither Jew nor Gentile, and thus the Jews and the Gentiles become one man in Christ. They are no longer in enmity, but peace and love prevail among them, and they all become a cause of peace for those around them.

2.15.0.en: Having slain the enmity thereby: by the death of Christ He trampled and slew the death resulting from sin, and so removed the enmity between man and God and also between the Jews and the Gentiles.

2.15.1.en: By Christ's redemption on the Cross, He gave the Jews and the Gentiles who believed in Him a new nature, so they became one together and were also united with God and became His body, that is, the Church, since Christ removed the sin that was a barrier between Him and man.

2.15.2.en: Sin is the cause of division among people, so repentance is what opens the way for love between you and others. In proportion to the love you show to every person, you prove that you are a Christian and a member of His body, and so you live in peace within yourself and spread peace and love among people.

2.16.0.en: Them that were nigh: the Jews.

2.16.1.en: Them that were afar off: the Gentiles.

2.16.2.en: Christ came preaching peace, fulfilling the saying of Isaiah the prophet (Isa 57:19), and the Apostles preached in His name, proclaiming peace and forgiveness to all peoples, Jews and Gentiles.

2.17.0.en: Christ brought us near to God, we Jews and Gentiles (1 Pet 3:18), so we obtained reconciliation with God and became, through Him and by the work of the Holy Spirit, part of His people. Here the work of the Holy Trinity in reconciliation appears: "through Him (Christ ....) in one Spirit (the Holy Spirit) to the Father."

2.18.0.en: Strangers: means lodgers, that is, temporary guests.

2.18.1.en: The estrangement was removed from the Gentiles by the redemptive work of Christ, and they became, together with the Jews who believed in Christ, one people; indeed they became so near that he calls them the household of God.

2.19.0.en: The building on which our faith stands has as its foundation the apostolic teaching that we received from the Apostles and of which the prophets prophesied, and it is the guide for the teaching of the Church and her whole life. The subject of the preaching of the Apostles and the prophets is Jesus Christ the Savior, whom St. Paul the Apostle likens to the cornerstone that binds the two walls meeting at right angles, which signify the Jews and the Gentiles, so they became one people when they believed in Christ.

2.20.0.en: In Christ the chief cornerstone the believers in Him are united, so they are like stones fitted together and fixed on the foundation, the chief cornerstone, that is, Christ. Indeed this building grows, that is, is sanctified as the temple of God by His dwelling in each one by His Holy Spirit and His dwelling in His Church through the Holy Sacraments.

2.21.0.en: Here the Apostle speaks of the whole Church together, including the Gentiles in Ephesus and the churches of Asia, saying that she becomes a holy temple for the dwelling of God, as he also said in (1 Cor 6:19), "Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you?"

2.21.1.en: May imitating the person of Christ be the basis of our conduct and our dealings, as He is the basis of our faith.

2.21.2.en: God's surpassing love in the salvation of the Gentiles
